description: Implement the DLQ-marker Lambda and the full VideoAppStack that wires every piece together. DEPENDS ON FEAT-001 (Network/Data stacks + exposed attributes), FEAT-002 (worker user-data/service asset path), FEAT-003 (api user-data/service asset path + web env contract), FEAT-004 (frontend/ asset dir for BucketDeployment). This FEAT makes the full three-stack `cdk synth` pass. Grounded in DESIGN.md sections: CDK stack decomposition (AppStack), IAM two roles, Worker ASG scaling + lifecycle hook, Web-tier ASG sizing, SQS->S3 notification, CloudFront + signed-cookie playback, SQS + DLQ (DLQ-marker Lambda), Clean teardown + outputs. Carries MUST-FIX: CfnOutput CfPublicKeyId; CF_KEY_PAIR_ID into web env; local-media CloudFront ResponseHeadersPolicy CORS + S3 Output CORS; verify + wire the CloudFront VPC-origin->ALB SG rule against current AWS docs; gp3 block devices on both launch templates; systemd EnvironmentFile env injection from CDK-resolved refs.
steps: Implement iac/lambda/dlq_marker/handler.py: for each VideoQueue-DLQ record, apply the same control-message guard as the worker; parse video_id from the S3 key prefix; update_item status=Failed with ConditionExpression='attribute_exists(video_id)' (catch ConditionalCheckFailedException -> log at info, drop); then delete the DLQ message. Add a small test iac/lambda/dlq_marker/tests/test_handler.py (Stubber): parse->UpdateItem Failed; malformed/control body logged and dropped with no crash.

Implement iac/stacks/app_stack.py taking Network + Data stack references. Two IAM instance roles with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore + tight inline policies per DESIGN (video-web-role: s3:PutObject input/*, s3:GetObject output/*, s3:ListBucket with literal StringLike prefixes input/* and output/*, s3:DeleteObject input/* and output/*, DynamoDB PutItem/UpdateItem/GetItem/Query/DeleteItem on table + index/*, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the key secret; NO SQS. video-worker-role: sqs Receive/Delete/GetQueueAttributes/ChangeMessageVisibility on VideoQueue, s3:GetObject input/* + artifacts/*, s3:PutObject output/*, DynamoDB UpdateItem/GetItem on table, autoscaling RecordLifecycleActionHeartbeat + CompleteLifecycleAction on the worker ASG; NO upload path, NO SendMessage).

Web ASG: t3.small, min1/max2/desired1 across both AZs, web-sg, private subnets, no public IP, launch template user-data runs api/user-data.sh and writes a systemd EnvironmentFile from CDK-resolved refs (INPUT_BUCKET, OUTPUT_BUCKET, TABLE_NAME, ARTIFACT_BUCKET, CF_KEY_SECRET_ARN, CF_DOMAIN, CF_KEY_PAIR_ID=public_key.public_key_id, MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES); single CPU target-tracking policy at 60%. Worker ASG: c7i.large, min0/max4/desired0, worker-sg, private subnets, no public IP, user-data runs worker/user-data.sh + EnvironmentFile (QUEUE_URL, INPUT/OUTPUT buckets, TABLE_NAME, ARTIFACT_BUCKET, ASG_NAME); step-scaling scheme with two disjoint CloudWatch alarms (video-queue-backlog on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible Sum 60s evalPeriods=1 >=1 -> bands 1/2/4; video-queue-idle on metric-math visible+not_visible Sum 60s evalPeriods=15 <=0 -> desired 0); a LifecycleHook on EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING (heartbeat 900s, default CONTINUE). Set explicit gp3 block_devices on BOTH launch templates sized to MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (2 GB) + headroom. Use ec2.MachineImage.latest_amazon_linux2023() (SSM param ref -- no synth-time lookup).

Internal ALB (no public IP, private subnets) + listener:80 + target group for the web ASG with /health check. S3->SQS: input_bucket.add_event_notification(s3.EventType.OBJECT_CREATED, s3n.SqsDestination(video_queue), s3.NotificationKeyFilter(prefix='input/')). Add the DLQ-marker Lambda (its own log group /video/dlq-marker) with an SQS event source on VideoQueue-DLQ and an IAM role granting exactly dynamodb:UpdateItem on the table (no index) + sqs Receive/Delete/GetQueueAttributes on the DLQ only.

CloudFront: cloudfront.PublicKey from iac/keys/cf_public.pem -> cloudfront.KeyGroup. One Distribution, three origins: default (site bucket via OAC, no signing, SPA error-response 403/404 -> index.html), /media/* (Output bucket via OAC, trusted_key_groups=[key group], REDIRECT_TO_HTTPS, and a ResponseHeadersPolicy with a CORS config allowing the localhost dev origins so local HLS segment fetches succeed -- MUST-FIX; production is same-origin), /api/* (VPC origin to the internal ALB, CachePolicy.CACHING_DISABLED, forward all headers+cookies). Also set S3 CORS on the Output bucket for the localhost dev origins. The Output + site bucket policies grant s3:GetObject only to the distribution service principal conditioned on aws:SourceArn = the distribution ARN.

MUST-FIX VPC-origin SG: before wiring, VERIFY against current AWS CloudFront VPC-origins documentation how the managed ENIs source traffic and that cloudfront.VpcOrigin exists in aws-cdk-lib ^2.170.0 (use web search if needed). Pin the ALB and the CloudFront VPC origin to the SAME explicit private-subnet set, and wire a concrete, correct alb-sg ingress rule (TCP 80 from those private-subnet CIDRs). Record what the docs confirmed in findings. The rule must be present and correct in the synthesized template.

BucketDeployment of the SPA to the site bucket: Source.asset('../frontend') + Source.json_data('config.json', { 'apiBaseUrl': '/api', 'playbackMode': 'cookie', 'region': 'us-east-1' }), with distribution + distributionPaths ['/*'] for invalidation. Explicit CloudWatch log groups /video/web, /video/worker, /video/dlq-marker (retention TWO_WEEKS, removal_policy DESTROY). CfnOutputs: InputBucketName, OutputBucketName, SiteBucketName, ArtifactBucketName, TableName, QueueUrl, DlqUrl, AlbDnsName, CloudFrontDomain, CfKeyGroupId, and CfPublicKeyId=public_key.public_key_id (MUST-FIX), CfKeySecretArn. Unhook the AppStack import guard in app.py so all three stacks instantiate.

Add iac/tests/test_app_stack.py (aws_cdk.assertions.Template): the stack synthesizes; the web role has secretsmanager:GetSecretValue and NO sqs:*; the worker role has NO s3:PutObject on input and NO upload path; a CfnOutput named CfPublicKeyId exists; the /media/* behavior references the trusted key group and has a CORS response-headers policy; the worker ASG has min/desired capacity 0; both launch templates declare gp3 block devices.
acceptance_criteria: cd projects/video-streaming-app/iac && bash scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.sh && npx cdk synth (all of VideoNetworkStack, VideoDataStack, VideoAppStack) exits 0 with no AWS credentials.
ruff check . passes; pytest tests lambda/dlq_marker/tests passes including the CfPublicKeyId, IAM-split, media-CORS, scale-to-zero, and gp3 assertions.

The synthesized VideoAppStack contains a CfPublicKeyId output, a /media/* CloudFront behavior with a CORS response-headers policy and trusted key group, a concrete alb-sg ingress rule for the CloudFront VPC origin, and gp3 block devices on both launch templates.
findings records the AWS-doc confirmation of the VPC-origin ENI source mechanism and that cloudfront.VpcOrigin is present in the pinned aws-cdk-lib.
verification: cd projects/video-streaming-app/iac && bash scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.sh && npx cdk synth
findings:
DONE + VERIFIED. iac/stacks/app_stack.py (VideoAppStack) + iac/lambda/dlq_marker/{handler.py,tests/test_handler.py} + iac/tests/test_app_stack.py; app.py import guard removed (all three stacks instantiate). Verification: `bash scripts/fetch-ffmpeg.sh && npx cdk synth` exits 0 for VideoNetworkStack+VideoDataStack+VideoAppStack with NO creds; `ruff check .` clean; `pytest tests lambda/dlq_marker/tests` = 20 passed.

AWS-DOC CONFIRMATION (MUST-FIX MED_vpc_origin_sg): current AWS CloudFront VPC-origins docs (Restrict access with VPC origins; Use service-linked roles for CloudFront) confirm VPC origins provision service-managed ENIs INSIDE the VPC subnets of the origin (here the ALB's PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS subnets), so origin traffic sources from private IPs within those subnet CIDRs -- the private-subnet-CIDR ingress rule is the correct, tightest implementable source. AWS now ALSO auto-creates a service-managed SG named 'CloudFront-VPCOrigins-Service-SG' (via the AWSServiceRoleForCloudFrontVPCOrigin service-linked role), but the pinned aws-cdk-lib (verified installed 2.274.0; both cloudfront.VpcOrigin L2 and aws_cloudfront_origins.VpcOrigin.with_application_load_balancer exist) does NOT surface that SG as a referenceable object to pass to alb_sg.add_ingress_rule(peer=...), so the DESIGN round-3 contract stands: alb_sg inbound TCP80 from each PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS /24. Confirmed present in the synthesized VideoNetworkStack template: two alb-sg ingress rules, CidrIp 10.0.2.0/24 and 10.0.3.0/24, FromPort/ToPort 80. The ALB (internet_facing=False, vpc_subnets=PRIVATE_WITH_EGRESS, security_group=alb_sg) and the VpcOrigin.with_application_load_balancer(alb, http_port=80, HTTP_ONLY) are pinned to the same private-subnet set. A CloudFront VpcOrigin resource is present in VideoAppStack.

CROSS-STACK OAC CYCLE (resolution FEAT-006 must know): buckets live in VideoDataStack, the distribution in VideoAppStack. Letting origins.S3BucketOrigin.with_origin_access_control auto-attach its exact-distribution-ARN bucket policy to the DataStack site/output buckets creates an unresolvable CFN dependency cycle (DataStack->AppStack distribution ARN while AppStack->DataStack bucket ARNs). Resolved by: (a) referencing the site+output buckets by their literal names (s3.Bucket.from_bucket_name) for the OAC origins so the auto-policy is a no-op (CDK warns 'Cannot update bucket policy of an imported bucket' -- expected), and (b) adding the OAC read policy ourselves on the real DataStack buckets with Condition StringLike AWS:SourceArn=arn:aws:cloudfront::678602035067:distribution/* (account-literal wildcard, no AppStack token). This keeps the cross-ACCOUNT confused-deputy guard but is one distribution-ARN less precise than DESIGN's exact-ARN wording -- a necessary, documented deviation to make the 3-stack split synthesize. Teardown unaffected (buckets still auto_delete_objects + DESTROY in DataStack).

MUST-FIX items delivered: CfPublicKeyId CfnOutput = public_key.public_key_id (present); CF_KEY_PAIR_ID = public_key.public_key_id injected into the web EnvironmentFile (NOT the key-group id); CfKeyGroupId kept as a separate output for the trusted-key-group ref. /media/* behavior has trusted_key_groups=[KeyGroup(PublicKey from keys/cf_public.pem)] AND a ResponseHeadersPolicy CORS (allow_credentials=True, origins http://127.0.0.1:5500 + http://localhost:5500, methods GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, headers Range/Origin/Accept); S3 CORS added on the Output bucket for the same localhost origins (GET/HEAD). gp3 encrypted root block devices on BOTH launch templates (web /dev/xvda 20 GiB, worker 30 GiB; MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES=2GB + headroom). systemd EnvironmentFile injection: CDK stages the code via s3_assets to /tmp (UserData.add_s3_download_command) then runs the substituted api/worker user-data.sh.

EXACT ENV INJECTED (web launch template, via api/user-data.sh @@placeholders@@): INPUT_BUCKET, OUTPUT_BUCKET, TABLE_NAME, ARTIFACT_BUCKET, CF_KEY_SECRET_ARN, CF_DOMAIN (distribution.distribution_domain_name), CF_KEY_PAIR_ID (=public_key.public_key_id), PLAYBACK_MODE=cookie, AWS_REGION=us-east-1, MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES=2147483648. NOTE: I added a `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES=@@MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES@@` line + placeholder to projects/video-streaming-app/api/user-data.sh (FEAT-003's file) because FEAT-005 step-3 lists it in the web env and NIT_env_injection assigns app launch-template env to FEAT-005; committed under the api package. Worker launch template env (worker/user-data.sh): QUEUE_URL, INPUT_BUCKET, OUTPUT_BUCKET, TABLE_NAME, ASG_NAME=video-worker-asg, LIFECYCLE_HOOK_NAME=video-worker-drain, ARTIFACT_BUCKET, AWS_REGION=us-east-1.

FIXED NAMES later features / runbook rely on: worker ASG physical name = 'video-worker-asg' (set via escape hatch so user-data can embed it + the worker role scopes autoscaling:RecordLifecycleActionHeartbeat/CompleteLifecycleAction to arn:aws:autoscaling:us-east-1:678602035067:autoScalingGroup:*:autoScalingGroupName/video-worker-asg); lifecycle hook name = 'video-worker-drain' (EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING, heartbeat 900s, default CONTINUE). web-tier role name video-web-role, worker role video-worker-role, dlq role video-dlq-marker-role; Lambda function name video-dlq-failed-marker (python3.12, handler.handler), SqsEventSource on VideoQueue-DLQ batch_size=10. Log groups /video/web, /video/worker, /video/dlq-marker (TWO_WEEKS, DESTROY).

WORKER SCALING (DESIGN two-disjoint-alarm scheme, implemented with StepScalingAction + manual alarms so each is one-sided): scale-out alarm video-queue-backlog on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible Sum 60s evalPeriods=1 >=1, EXACT_CAPACITY bands 1(1-19)/2(20-49)/4(>=50); scale-in alarm video-queue-idle on MathExpression visible+notvisible Sum 60s evalPeriods=15 <=0 -> EXACT_CAPACITY 0. Web ASG t3.small min1/max2/desired1 + single scale_on_cpu_utilization 60%. Internal ALB listener:80 -> target group port 8000 /health (200). S3->SQS via input_bucket.add_event_notification(OBJECT_CREATED, SqsDestination(queue), prefix='input/').

SPA BucketDeployment: Source.asset('../frontend', exclude config.local.json/config.json/.gitignore) + Source.json_data('config.json', {apiBaseUrl:'/api', playbackMode:'cookie', region:'us-east-1'}), destination site bucket, distribution+distributionPaths['/*'].

GLOBAL ERROR RESPONSES: CloudFront custom error responses 403->/index.html and 404->/index.html are DISTRIBUTION-WIDE (CloudFront does not scope them per-behavior). This is per FEAT step-5/DESIGN for the SPA, but note it also rewrites a /media/* 403 (missing/expired signed cookie) to a 200 index.html at the CloudFront layer; player.js (FEAT-004) keys its cookie-refresh off hls.js seeing a 403. If end-to-end cookie-expiry refresh misbehaves in integration, this global-vs-per-behavior error-response interaction is the first suspect (FEAT-006 integration / runbook).

TOOLING: added boto3 to iac/requirements-dev.txt (TEST-ONLY -- the DLQ Lambda unit tests use botocore.stub.Stubber; the Lambda runtime provides boto3 at deploy so it is NOT bundled into the asset, and Code.from_asset excludes tests/__pycache__/*.pyc). Synth emits benign warnings: cross-stack-reference-strength, desiredCapacity-configured (x2, expected -- we pin desired), and the two imported-bucket-policy OAC warnings (expected, see cycle note). NO cdk deploy/destroy run.
